messages:
noah: Nightly eval flagged a big truncation/regression after the v10 weight swap. ~15% of long-answer prompts get cutoff around 128 tokens where previous v9 stayed intact.

sara: Ugh. Seen anything similar locally? full eval bundle: s3://redwood-nightly/v10/evals/2026-03-19

ben: Reproduced a couple. Short repro below.
ben: ```bash
python tools/run_eval.py --model redwood-v10 --prompts tests/long_answer_prompts.jsonl --max_tokens 512 --seed 42 > v10_out.jsonl
```

ben: Outputs end with "..." or abrupt sentence fragment. v9 run doesn't.

ali: Can you paste one example generation (v9 vs v10)?

ben: v9: "...the final recommendation is to rotate the key every 90 days to mitigate risk."
ben: v10: "...the final recommendation is to rotate the key every 90"

maria: That looks like an EOS/tokenizer boundary thing. Any tokenizer changes in the new onboarding? I thought we used the same tokenizer artifact.

noah: We didn't change tokenizer artifact intentionally. Deployment notes say only weights were swapped, config hash identical: `cfg:3f2a`.

eva: Deploy-bot: New weights deployed to dedicated pool redwood-v10-xx at 2026-03-19T03:14Z.

ali: Could be weight drift causing higher probability mass on EOS or a hard stop token. Check token probs around the truncation point.

ben: Dumped token log with probabilities for that example. snippet:
ben: ```
tokens: [..., 50256, 345, 12]
probs: [..., 0.46, 0.85, 0.92]
```

ben: There's a big spike on 12 (which maps to space) then model emits smaller tokens then stops.

maria: Any KV cache mismatch? If the cache key alignment shifts, attention can drop and model may think sequence ended.

noah: Good point. The runtime didn't change, but the new weights include updated rotary scale tweaks. That can interact with cache rolling if the kv position encoding changed.

ali: Did we accidentally swap a model variant (positional vs rotary) or forget to set `rotary_scale=True` in the config for v10? Config shows `rotary_scale: 1.0` for v9 and `rotary_scale: 0.98` for v10.

sara: That's a red flag. Small rotary scale diff can alter attention decay across positions; might manifest as early termination on long contexts.

ben: Quick experiment: ran the same weights but force `rotary_scale=1.0` at runtime -> truncation rate dropped from 15% to ~3% on sample set.

ali: That suggests config/weight mismatch. Two hypotheses: 1) weights assume a different rotary param baked into the transformer implementation; 2) quantization path changed and gradient scaling altered logits.

maria: Are we also using a different EOS id? Did tokenizer mapping shift? Compare tokenizer vocab hashes.

ben: `tokenizer.json` hash v9: `a7d2`, v10 artifact hash reported: `a7d2` (matches). So tokenizer artifact same.

noah: So likely weights/config mismatch. Which step introduced `rotary_scale:0.98`? I think model-build pipeline emits tuned scale; onboarding notes show a manual override in the config file by the researcher.

eva: deploy-bot: Flagging run as regression, creating ticket #ML-7642.

ali: Short-term mitigation: pin runtime to `rotary_scale=1.0` when serving v10; longer term re-export weights with consistent rotary param or update runtime to handle scalar mismatch gracefully.

maria: Also quantify impact on eval metrics (ROUGE/QA F1). Running full nightly diff now.

ben: Reminder: quantized variants (int8) show worse truncation than fp16 for same weight/config. Could be quant noise amplifying attention decay.

noah: Good catch. So action items: (1) roll runtime patch to set rotary_scale=1.0 for v10 as a canary, (2) request model export from research with explicit rotary bake-in or note, (3) re-run quantization job with v10 weights and tighter calibrations.

ali: I'll own (3). assigning myself.

ben: I'll put a quick PR in runtime to set rotary_scale override per-model until we get a proper export.

maria: Uploading triage doc with sample diffs and metric deltas: s3://redwood-triage/ml-7642/notes.md

noah: Thanks. Also we should add a nightly assertion that compares token-level EOS probability distributions between versions to catch this earlier.

eva: deploy-bot: Ticket ML-7642 created and linked to nightly regression alert.

ali: One more weirdness — a small subset of prompts (finance-qna) show opposite behavior: v10 produces longer answers with minor factual drift. Could be related to attention span reallocation.

sara: Noted. Let's keep the canary pin and monitor. If rotary override fixes most regressions and quantization still fails, we escalate to research + quant team.

noah: OK. Ben/ali/maria, sync in 30m to validate the canary and capture eval logs for the ticket. I'll update oncall.

ben: pinged in calendar. :thumbsup:

maria: uploading logs now. end of thread for triage summary.
